selection.strategy: next 10 municipalities after Asten; official-source review with expired-regulation detection and address-level fallbacks

findings: Current pre-mantelzorg policy explicitly distinguishes inwoning from permanent dwelling splitting and room rental; those latter uses are not permitted through that policy route.

The current Omgevingsprogramma wonen states that the municipality intends to create an assessment framework for dwelling splitting and room rental, showing that these uses require separate spatial-policy assessment rather than a generic permitted conclusion.
Address-level omgevingsplan review remains required for ordinary room rental or splitting.
The former Huisvestingsverordening Baarn 2023 expired on 3 November 2025 and must not be used for 2026 answers.
It was replaced by the current Huisvestingsverordening regio Amersfoort – gemeente Baarn, valid from 3 November 2025 through 30 September 2032 with retroactive effect from 3 July 2025.
The current regulation primarily governs housing allocation/permits; use changes still require spatial/address-level review where relevant.
The 2020 regional housing-allocation regulation expired on 1 July 2024 and is not current evidence.
The current Verordening Woonruimtebemiddeling regio Rotterdam 2025 applies from 1 July 2025 through 30 June 2029.
The current Omgevingsplan gemeente Barendrecht is also in force; room rental, splitting and non-standard residential use therefore remain address/use-specific spatial questions.
The 2024-2028 regulation expired on 29 April 2025 and has been replaced by Huisvestingsverordening Barneveld 2025-2029.
The current regulation contains permit rules for conversion of self-contained housing to non-self-contained housing and for splitting dwellings, with scope tied to WOZ/NHG and geographic conditions.
Applications are assessed for housing-stock interests and liveability including parking, noise, fire safety, social safety and privacy.
The Westelijke Mijnstreek 2025 rental ordinance is current in Beek and requires a municipal rental permit for all accommodation used for housing labour migrants.
The explanatory material also notes that many room-rental situations can conflict with the omgevingsplan, so a rental permit does not replace spatial-use approval.
Ordinary room rental/splitting outside this labour-migrant regime still requires targeted omgevingsplan review.
Beleidsregel kamerverhuur en woningsplitsing Beekdaelen 2024 is current from 29 February 2024.
It explicitly addresses room rental and dwelling splitting and links decisions to the spatial framework/parapluplan and liveability considerations.
Address-level plan compatibility remains necessary before a definitive outcome.
Huisvestingsverordening Beesel 2026 is current from 1 July 2026 through 30 June 2030.
Its confirmed scope includes a house-permit system for available social rental homes owned by housing corporations, with defined exclusions.
This regulation is allocation-focused; it should not be treated as a complete answer for room rental, splitting or other spatial-use changes.
Current Bibob policy identifies room-rental/logies businesses with five or more rooms as a risk category for relevant permits, confirming that such uses can require permitting scrutiny.
No current dedicated Huisvestingsverordening/opkoopbescherming regime was established in this pass.
No unrestricted conclusion may be drawn; exact room-rental/splitting legality must be checked against the applicable omgevingsplan and permit route.

The former policy for better use of the existing housing stock, which contained explicit rules for splitting, double occupancy and room rental, expired on 1 July 2025 and cannot be used as current 2026 legal authority.

Because that former policy shows these activities have historically been regulated spatially, current legality must now be established from the current omgevingsplan/current successor policy rather than copied from the expired policy.
Targeted successor-policy and address-level omgevingsplan review remain required.
Huisvestingsverordening Bergen (L) 2026 is current from 1 July 2026 through 30 June 2030.
The confirmed ordinance regulates the housing-permit/allocation system for designated social rental housing in the regional North Limburg framework.
It does not by itself resolve room-rental, splitting or other spatial-use changes; address-level omgevingsplan review remains required for those topics.
